info.name: UW Risk Agent — /assess
info.description:
Twelve submissions for POST /assess on the underwriting API.

Cases 09/10 are a matched pair: identical High flood band, differing
only in build year either side of the Flood Re 2009 cut-off. Cases 11/12
separate the HIGH crime band (loading) from VERY_HIGH (referral).

Each case isolates one decision driver where possible, and the
postcodes were verified against the live tools rather than
invented — flood bands come from the EA RoFRS dataset, crime from
data.police.uk, sale prices from HM Land Registry, and claims from
the mock register in risk_server_v4.py.

Prerequisites:
  ./start.sh   (MCP :8001, API :8010)

Expected outcomes are in each request's description. They are the
underwriting intent, not assertions — the agent applies judgement,
so a borderline case may legitimately land one band away. The
tests only check the response shape.

Each request takes roughly 15-40s: the agent calls MCP tools in a
loop before deciding. Raise Postman's timeout if needed.

item.name: 09 High flood + Flood Re + resilience — REFER or DECLINE

body.raw:
{
  "applicant_name": "Alice Jones",

  "prior_claim_types": [
    "theft"
  ],
  "outstanding_claims": false,
  "broker_reference": "BRK-2026-00109",
  "special_conditions": "Flood resilience measures installed 2022: raised electrics, solid concrete floor with sealed membrane, flood doors and airbrick covers. Certificate available on request."
}

request.description:
Teddington, on the tidal Thames. RoFRS reports High (>1 in 30 annual
chance) and flood_re_eligible is true. Built 1985, before the Flood Re
cut-off of 1 January 2009, and flood resilience measures are declared in
special_conditions.

Crime is LOW (108/mo, 0.4x the London median), construction is brick and
there is one minor claim — flood is the only adverse signal, which makes
this a clean test of the Flood Re escape route.

Guideline 3.1 says High risk is declined UNLESS Flood Re cession applies
AND the property has flood resilience measures. Both conditions are met
here, so the guideline points to a Flood Re referral.

In practice this case is unstable: repeated runs return REFER and
DECLINE on the same payload. The agent is weighing whether resilience
measures genuinely offset a >1 in 30 flood probability, which is a
legitimate judgement call rather than a defect. Compare with case 10,
which removes the Flood Re route entirely and declines consistently.

Expected outcome: REFER (DECLINE also observed and defensible)

exec: console.log('09 High flood, Flood Re eligible — expect REFER ->', d.decision, d.confidence, '|', (d.risk_flags||[]).join(', '));

request.description:
Brixton. 954 property crimes/month within ~1 mile, about 3.4x the
median London postcode — the HIGH band (busier than roughly 75% of
London, but below the VERY_HIGH threshold of 1459).

Flood is Very Low, construction is brick and there are no claims, so
crime is isolated.

This case is deliberately borderline. Guideline 6 puts HIGH at a 10%
buildings loading with minimum security requirements, and guideline 7
lists only VERY HIGH as a mandatory referral — so the written rules
point to ACCEPT with a loading. In practice the agent refers, citing
crime above its automatic acceptance threshold, which the system prompt
permits: it instructs the agent to apply judgement and names borderline
crime as a REFER trigger.

Both outcomes are underwriting-defensible. The case is included to show
where the agent is more cautious than the letter of the guidelines, not
to assert one correct answer.

Expected outcome: REFER (ACCEPT with 10% loading also acceptable)

exec: console.log('11 High crime band — expect ACCEPT with loading ->', d.decision, d.confidence, '|', (d.risk_flags||[]).join(', '));

request.description:
Soho. 2748 property crimes/month within ~1 mile, about 9.9x the median
London postcode — the highest exposure in this collection and well
into the VERY_HIGH band (top ~10%, threshold 1459).

A ground-floor flat with contents cover and a prior theft claim
compounds it. Guideline 6 requires a senior underwriter referral and
an enhanced security survey at this band. Flood is Very Low, so crime
drives the decision on its own.

Expected outcome: REFER — senior underwriter, enhanced security survey

exec: console.log('12 Extreme crime exposure — expect REFER ->', d.decision, d.confidence, '|', (d.risk_flags||[]).join(', '));
